overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to periodically review executive session minutes and by missing the 10-day response deadline and production of missing minutes; redactions were upheld and the pre-July 2010 roll call allegation was declined.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly failed to periodically review executive session minutes to decide on release; reviews began only in May 2014.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee's failure to periodically review its executive session minutes violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly failed to respond within 10 days to a September 2014 request for executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: the Committee's failure to respond to Mr. Harris' request for executive session minutes within 10 days violated the law.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly failed to maintain and produce three executive session minutes that were missing when the requested set was released.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee's failure to produce these minutes within the time period required by law violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly improperly redacted portions of four sets of executive session minutes released to the requester.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by redacting portions of these minutes when it originally produced them

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged executive session minutes from 2007 to 2009 fail to record roll call votes as required by law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review the allegation that the Committee failed to record roll call votes during executive sessions held prior to that date

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
